transcription_convention: Cipher letters are copied from each edition. Editorial word division, long s and doubtful type are explained for the individual item.

key-numeral-cipher.normalized_latin: Iaaihid ifeib, ieifeigeicchkib. cakeihid. i&kahk. gidibid. eigih. ieeigigh ibkig. &kif. iaaihifid, ibeicdaka eih. icei&kaib.
key-numeral-cipher.reason: The type on C ii verso gives i&kahk, &kif and icei&kaib. C ii recto assigns the cipher group i& to q and the single ampersand to f. The open-foot h can be distinguished from the closed b in the same lines. The inter-group punctuation is regularized and the line breaks are represented by spaces. The unusual i&kahk is transcribed as printed. The source footer identifies HAB images 535 (key) and 536 (example), corpus images 529 and 530. The independently digitized BSB copy of this setting agrees.

key-numeral-alphabet.reason: The numeral key assigns the bare ampersand to plaintext f (6) and i& to plaintext q (16). Both entries use the sign as part of the cipher.
